contributions.statement: Before untrusted third-party code (vendor SDKs, external snippets, issue attachments) enters agent context, strip or neutralize comments, string literals and decoy blocks with a Tree-sitter pass; this cut indirect-injection success about 3x on three hosted models but left a 6-8% residual, so keep sandboxing and permissions too.
contributions.evidence: §4.2 RQ4 Table 2: ASR 27.11->7.72 (Claude-3.5-Haiku), 18.32->5.81 (GPT-5.1-Codex-mini), 24.14->8.28 (Gemini-3.1-Flash-lite); base models, not agents; full method also uses surrogate-model logits; not shown on Java.
relative_to: input sanitization / spotlighting for prompt injection (P22)

contributions.statement: Do not apply such sanitization to your own trusted repositories, because blanket sanitization cut repository-level completion exact match by about 33 points.
contributions.evidence: §4.2 RQ5 Table 3: RepoBench EM -32.67 (BLEU-4 -5.95), MBPP -6.23; victim model not stated.

reason: Gives a measured, cheap structural pre-filter for untrusted code context and a measured cost when applied too broadly; the adaptive-attack robustness claim is weak and is not used.
